author: Dylan Owen (Design & Production)

licence_note: Third-party rulebook PDF. Not committed to the repo (research/sources/**/original.pdf is gitignored). source.md is a full page-by-page verbatim text extraction, kept for internal research reproducibility and citation only — it is quoted from, never reproduced wholesale, in the vault note.
designer_statement_note: The rulebook is the publisher's own primary rules text — the direct source, not a secondary summary.

extraction_method.reason: Clean embedded text layer confirmed across all 164 pages (avg text well above the 120 char/page OCR threshold).
extraction_method.encoding_check: Full extraction scanned for U+FFFD (replacement character): 0 found across all 164 pages.

probe_note: Ross's earlier keyword probe found 'robot' x110, 'campaign' x73, 'perp' x54, 'hacking' x3, 'stealth' x3 across the book. Full read confirms campaign/perp/sentencing hits were real mechanical density (see vault note). The robot count was largely repetitive flavour text and a single repeated one-line special rule ('Robot') stamped on every robot profile — NOT 110 distinct mechanical touchpoints. Hacking and stealth are each a single Armoury-card item, not subsystems. See vault note for detail.
important_correction: block-war.pdf in this source folder was originally assumed to be a supplement to THIS rulebook (Warlord Games 2020). It is not. Its own copyright page reads '(c)2013 Rebellion Developments Ltd... www.mongoosepublishing.com... Revised 16th April 2013' and its rules use Credits/Rep/Minions/Heroes/Experience Points terminology with no Notoriety, Action chips, or Combat dice anywhere in the text -- a completely different, older Judge Dredd miniatures game published by Mongoose (c.2009-2013), not a Warlord Games product. See block-war-meta.json in this folder for detail. It was NOT used as a source for the Judge Dredd Miniatures Game vault note.
